problem: Prior embodied referring expression grounding methods (e.g. DUET) concatenate discrete view and candidate object embeddings and process them with the same vanilla FFN encoder, giving ambiguous representations even though views and objects differ in distribution and serve different subtasks (navigation vs. object grounding).
motivation: Views give room layout and global context while objects give fine item detail. Views are used for sequential navigation decisions and objects for grounding at the destination, so this is a multi-input, multi-task problem. Shared FFNs blur these differences, and sparse MoE could specialize processing per visual type.
key_idea: Replace the dense FFNs in DUET's panorama and local cross-modal encoders with sparse MoE layers whose router input is augmented with learnable view/object type embeddings (visual-aware routing).
insight: Plain SMoE gives a modest gain (SR 46.98 to 48.37 on REVERIE val unseen), while adding visual-aware routing gives a much larger one (SR 49.92 without the aux loss), so type-conditioned routing is the main contributor. Gains grow as more layers are converted (Table 6), and 4 experts with top-2 is the sweet spot: top-1 and 16 experts hurt SPL. The larger RGSPL gain on SOON is attributed to its many more candidate objects per step (45.8 vs 3.42).
method: Base model: DUET-style dual-scale planner with a language encoder, a 2-layer panorama encoder over views and objects, and local/global cross-modal encoders; the topological map is used for global reasoning.
Sparse MoE layer: replaces the FFN with N expert FFNs and a top-k softmax router, and the output is the gate-weighted sum of the k selected experts.

Visual-aware routing: adds a learnable type embedding (b_v for views, b_o for objects) to the token before the router, G(x)=topk(softmax(W_g(x+b_t))), so views and objects are routed to different experts.
Placement: MoE layers are inserted in the panorama encoder (2 layers) and the 4-layer local-scale cross-modal encoder; the cross-modal experts are initialized from LXMERT FFN weights.
Auxiliary load-balancing loss (alpha=0.001) prevents expert collapse.
Training: pre-training with MLM, MRC, SAP, OG and Aux; fine-tuning with SAP, DAgger, OG and Aux.

setting.backbone: DUET-style transformer with ViSMoE layers (4 experts, top-2), cross-modal encoders initialized from LXMERT; trained/fine-tuned
setting.training_data: REVERIE and SOON training sets with the standard DUET pre-training tasks (MLM, MRC, SAP, OG); no extra data stated
setting.observation: panoramic discrete views plus candidate object features (annotated bounding boxes on REVERIE)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints plus stop, then object selection from candidates
setting.privileged: none beyond the benchmark-standard annotated object bounding boxes / candidate objects

results: On REVERIE val unseen, ViSMoE reaches SR 50.18 and RGS 33.71 versus DUET's 46.98 and 32.15, and it also improves on test unseen (SR 54.16, RGS 33.38). It beats FDA on SR and RGS but not on SPL or RGSPL on val unseen. On SOON it improves over DUET on all metrics, with val-unseen SPL 26.13 vs 22.58 and test RGSPL 5.20 vs 4.17. Its val-unseen SR of 38.23 edges KERM's 38.05 and GridMM's 37.46.
limitations: Gains on SOON test are small (SPL +0.11), and the REVERIE val-unseen SPL and RGSPL do not beat FDA.
Only evaluated on REVERIE and SOON in simulation, with no real robot; more experts or higher top-k increase compute without gains.
Ablations are done only on REVERIE val unseen, and parameter counts and compute costs are not reported.
